problem: Waypoint-only navigation policies (ViNT, NoMaD) lack visual foresight, while navigation world models (NWM) need one costly video rollout per candidate trajectory. Existing navigation world-action models are either autoregressive, rely on rollouts, or lack metric geometric supervision.
motivation: Humans anticipate how the scene and goal look from future viewpoints, which gives an interpretable basis for action selection. A single generative process that outputs both futures and actions could be efficient enough for real-time use. Pretrained video diffusion priors plus geometry supervision could make this scalable, including from video-only data.
key_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained Wan2.1-1.3B video diffusion transformer to jointly denoise future-video latents, waypoint tokens and geometry-aware camera tokens under one flow-matching objective, with a Fast variant that drops image tokens at inference.
insight: Camera-token denoising (from a frozen DA3 geometry model) is what lets video-only data help: without it, adding video-only data worsens ATE by 0.009 (0.321 to 0.330), with it ATE and RPE both drop by 0.012 (0.314 to 0.302). Asymmetric attention lets Fast keep foresight supervision in training but reach similar accuracy without image tokens, halving latency (0.389 s to 0.212 s at 2 steps). More denoising steps do not improve accuracy monotonically.
method: Unified token sequence: [camera | future-video | trajectory | history | goal | register] tokens processed by one Wan2.1 DiT; visual tokens keep RoPE, while trajectory, camera and register tokens get identity positional encodings.
Waypoint tokens: K=6 continuous (dx, dy, dyaw) waypoints in the local frame, projected by an MLP and decoded by a light trajectory head.
Geometry-aware camera tokens: a frozen Depth Anything 3 (DA3) model extracts normalized camera tokens for future views; these are noised and denoised as an auxiliary target (MLP_c).
Unified flow-matching loss: L = λvid·mvid·Lvid + λtraj·mtraj·Ltraj (SmoothL1) + λcam·mcam·Lcam, with λ = 1/5/0.01 and per-sample masks that allow video-only samples (mtraj=0).
Mixed data training: trajectory-labeled navigation data plus video-only 3D datasets (ScanNet, DL3DV, CityWalker, LAVN) that supervise only the video and camera losses.
UniNav-Full: jointly denoises future video, trajectory and camera tokens, and decodes RGB foresight.

UniNav-Fast: trained as a separate model with an asymmetric attention mask so non-future tokens cannot attend to noisy future-video tokens; future-video tokens are removed at inference, skipping video denoising and VAE decoding.

setting.backbone: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B video diffusion transformer (fine-tuned) with frozen Wan VAE and frozen DA3 geometry model
setting.training_data: Trajectory-labeled navigation data from RECON, SACSoN, GO Stanford and SCAND (main comparison uses only these); optional video-only ScanNet, DL3DV, CityWalker and LAVN for the mixed-data ablation
setting.observation: 3 history egocentric RGB frames plus a goal image, resized to 256x192
setting.action_space: K=6 continuous local waypoints (Δx, Δy, Δyaw), predicted offline

numbers.extra: navigation data only, 2 sampling steps, latency 0.212 s

numbers_note: Split names are not stated in the paper. 'test' is assumed for the four offline datasets. Table 1 also lists Avg. (Full 0.491/0.155; Fast 0.492/0.160), GO Stanford Full (0.722/0.110), SACSoN Fast (0.490/0.166) and SCAND Fast (0.474/0.250). Those rows are not listed individually above.
results: UniNav achieves the best ATE on all four datasets, with reductions of 3.7% on RECON, 24.7% on SaCSoN, 18.2% on GO Stanford and 6.8% on SCAND versus the strongest baseline (NWM or ViNT). Average ATE is 0.491 (Full) versus 0.593 for NWM and 0.659 for ViNT. Fast at 1 step has 0.109 s latency (ATE 0.318 on RECON), versus about 900 s and 12,000 NFE for NWM.
limitations: Only short-horizon local waypoint prediction; no long-horizon planning.
Evaluation is offline on datasets; no closed-loop or robot deployment in the main results.
Latency (0.1 s at best) is still far above ViNT (0.015 s).
